cold_email.subject: Interest in Educator / Del Amo (Full-Time) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Educator / Del Amo (Full-Time) opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Research Coordinator 1 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Worldwide Clinical Trials Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Research Coordinator 1 opportunity with Worldwide Clinical Trials at Worldwide Clinical Trials.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.body:
Dear The University of Texas at San Antonio Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Enterprise Programmer Analyst opportunity with The University of Texas at San Antonio at The University of Texas at San Antonio.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Special Education Aide (6.25 hrs/day) (3 positions available) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear SchoolSpring Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Special Education Aide (6.25 hrs/day) (3 positions available) opportunity with SchoolSpring at SchoolSpring.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in IS Support Tech-Full Time — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Intermountain Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the IS Support Tech-Full Time opportunity with Intermountain Hospital at Intermountain Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in IS Support Tech-Full Time — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Havenwyck Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the IS Support Tech-Full Time opportunity with Havenwyck Hospital at Havenwyck Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Academic Instructor, Substitute On Call — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Career Systems Development Corp Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Academic Instructor, Substitute On Call opportunity with Career Systems Development Corp at Career Systems Development Corp.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Associate — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Bruker Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Associate opportunity with Bruker at Bruker.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator - 001251 opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

cold_email.body:
Dear AMG School of Nursing Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Registrar opportunity with AMG School of Nursing at AMG School of Nursing.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Life Science Research Professional 1 (On-Site Only) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Stanford University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Life Science Research Professional 1 (On-Site Only) opportunity with Stanford University at Stanford University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Lab Analyst I opportunity with Jacobs at Jacobs.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Assistant Program Coordinator Trainee - The Women's Resource Center — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear California State University-Sacramento Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Assistant Program Coordinator Trainee - The Women's Resource Center opportunity with California State University-Sacramento at California State University-Sacramento.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in AI/ML Research Associate — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Analytical Mechanics Associates Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the AI/ML Research Associate opportunity with Analytical Mechanics Associates at Analytical Mechanics Associates.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Behavior Analyst in Training - Paradise Valley — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Soar Autism Center Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Behavior Analyst in Training - Paradise Valley opportunity with Soar Autism Center at Soar Autism Center.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Process Data Engineer I - Pharmaceutical Product Development
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Build the data foundation that helps us get to an AI native state Advanced AI is only as powerful as the data that enables it. We are seeking an early-career Data Engineer passionate about creating high-quality scientific data products and contributing to the development of data fabric to support advanced analytics, AI, machine learning, and scientific decision-making across Pharmaceutical Product Development. The ideal candidate will be an engineer who sees data not as a collection of tables, but as a strategic asset that powers scientific discovery and AI innovation. This role will provide an opportunity to work on complex datasets, modern cloud technologies, and cutting-edge digital transformation initiatives, with applications across chemical process development, biologics development, drug product development, and analytical development. What You Will Do Build scientific data products for product development focused on datasets for molecular features, material properties, laboratory data, process and manufacturing parameters, stability and product performance data. Contribute to initiatives for data structuring and data contextualization. Develop and maintain scalable data pipelines supporting analytics, AI, and scientific modelling initiatives. Transform raw scientific and operational data into trusted, model-ready data products. Work with cross-functional teams to improve data accessibility, reliability, and quality. Support enterprise initiatives involving Databricks, Data Fabric, and cloud-native architectures. Automate data workflows and reduce manual effort through engineering best practices. Contribute to development of reusable data assets supporting Product Development innovation across US, Europe and India. What Makes You Successful You are naturally curious and: Ask why before asking how. Investigate root causes rather than treating symptoms. Enjoy solving messy, ambiguous data problems. Balance technical rigor with practical execution. Work effectively with scientists, analysts, data scientists, and engineers. Qualifications Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Chemical Engineering, Information Systems, Bioinformatics, Biotechnology or related field with 2+ years of industry experience. Technical hands-on experience with modern data technologies. Data Engineering: SQL, Python, ETL/ELT Development, Delta Lake, Lakehouse Architecture, Medallion Architecture, Data Modelling, Data Warehousing, Distributed Computing, Data Validation Cloud & Modern Data Platforms: Databricks, dbt, AWS Modern Data Practices: Data Product Design, Vector Databases, Data Quality Engineering, Data Observability, Metadata Management, Master Data Management, Data Lineage, Data Governance principles, Data Cataloguing Emerging Technologies: AI-Ready Data Foundations, Vector Database fundamentals, Semantic Layer Design, Knowledge Graph Concepts, Data Foundations for GenAI & Agentic AI Applications Software Engineering & Delivery Practices: Git & Version Control, API Integration, Workflow Automation, CI/CD Fundamentals, Agile Delivery Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and collaboration abilities. Preferred Experience working with pharmaceutical product development datasets in the scientific, manufacturing, or laboratory data domains Exposure to scientific, analytical, or laboratory-based methods through academic coursework, research with an aptitude for understanding the data generated by these techniques Familiarity with Data products and AI/ML workflows Experience with PySpark, Python, SQL, dbt, Databricks We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. How We Work Where you work matters – because collaboration, innovation and patient impact happen in many settings. Our roles are structured across four work models: site-essential, site-by-design, field-based and remote-by-design. The model assigned to this role is based on its core responsibilities. Learn more at https://careers.bms.com/ways-of-working. Supporting People with Disabilities BMS is dedicated to ensuring that people with disabilities can excel through a transparent recruitment process, reasonable workplace accommodations/adjustments and ongoing support in their roles. Applicants can request a reasonable workplace accommodation/adjustment prior to accepting a job offer. If you require reasonable accommodations/adjustments in completing this application, or in any part of the recruitment process, direct your inquiries to adastaffingsupport@bms.com . cold_email.subject: Interest in Process Data Engineer I - Pharmaceutical Product Development — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Process Data Engineer I - Pharmaceutical Product Development opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Produce Clerk — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Kroger Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Produce Clerk opportunity with Kroger at Kroger.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. jobs.description: 2027 Process Development Rotation Program (2 years) Department Summary This role is a valuable part of Pharmaceutical Technical Development (PTD), dedicated to advancing Genentech's protein pharmaceutical pipeline from discovery to commercialization. As a member of this organization, you will have the opportunity to engage in innovative process development, formulation, and analytical method optimization while collaborating closely with multidisciplinary teams. Your contributions will be crucial in delivering novel medicines that meet the critical needs of patients. This position is based in South San Francisco, on site . The Opportunity Process Development Rotation Program (PDRP) offers associates the opportunity to experience four diverse six-month assignments over the course of two years within various areas of the process development organization (see more here ). In this program, you will have the opportunity to: Experience working on meaningful projects: directly support a molecule, explore a complex scientific question, or evaluate and implement new technologies, supporting areas such as: cell culture development, purification development, analytical development & protein characterization, and drug product process development. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to optimize our current processes and technologies. Engage in hands-on lab work and rigorous data analysis. Actively participate in professional development committees within the PDRP organization. Build a cross-functional network across our process development group. Who You Are Required Education Recent graduates (less than two years from the program start date) with a B.S., B.A., or M.S. degree. Required Disciplines Chemical engineering, biochemical engineering, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, biomedical engineering, bioengineering, microbiology, biology, or related disciplines. Knowledge, Skills, and Qualifications Passionate about science and engineering, data-driven, and enjoy the challenges associated with complex problem-solving. Highly self-motivated and willing to work independently or as part of multi-disciplinary teams. Demonstrated leadership experience in academic, extracurricular, or professional settings (e.g., leading a club, team projects, or other initiatives). Strong critical thinking, verbal and written communication, and collaboration skills. Preferred Experience Experience working in research labs or industrial internships. Experience working with biologics (proteins, cells, mRNA, DNA) and related technical skills. The expected hourly rate for this position based on the primary location of California is $44.72 . Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law. This position also qualifies for the benefits detailed at the link provided below. Benefits Notes: Relocation benefits are available for those that qualify. The target start date for this position is August 2027. Genentech is an equal opportunity employer. It is our policy and practice to employ, promote, and otherwise treat any and all employees and applicants on the basis of merit, qualifications, and competence. The company's policy prohibits unlawful discrimination, including but not limited to, discrimination on the basis of Protected Veteran status, individuals with disabilities status, and consistent with all federal, state, or local laws. If you have a disability and need an accommodation in relation to the online application process, please contact us by completing this form Accommodations for Applicants .

jobs.title: Product Manager, Global Medical Affairs BI&T - Scientific Content & Publications
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Position Responsibilities Product Manager, Global Medical Affairs Business Insights & Technology (BI&T) - Scientific Content & Publications is accountable for the product management & effective delivery of BI&T capabilities and services supporting Global Medical Affairs Medical Communications Teams at BMS, positioning BMS Medical Affairs for success in the digital era. This role partners with stakeholders in the BMS Medical Excellence Team, Therapeutic Area Teams along with the BI&T Content Capabilities Team and Worldwide Commercialization Excellence team to define and drive digital capabilities in the areas of Scientific Content and Publications. This position has a focus on understanding requirements and enabling capabilities such as Content usage/value metrics, Componentized and AI-generated Content, Content localization for international markets, Publications management, and integration of key content and publications data within relevant workflows. The vision of the Medical Affairs organization is to transform lives through patient-driven science. You will be expected to lead and accelerate Medical’s digitization through technology innovation, ensure that their information capabilities and operations are reliable, accessible and secure, and enable them to become competitively differentiated in a rapidly-changing complex scientific landscape. You will partner closely with matrix teams across the Enterprise to drive digital capabilities across Medical Affairs with an enterprise mindset. You will build strong partnerships with designated Medical leadership teams to drive adoption of digital capabilities and innovation opportunities. Provide domain leadership: Owns the Technology Roadmap: Drives the development of realistic and actionable multi-year strategic digital capability roadmaps, informed and jointly-aligned with the associated business process owners and Analytics counterparts. Prioritizes the portfolio appropriately and is accountable for the overall portfolio Execution, even if not always responsible for delivery. Intimately understands the data (quality, location, and value) that informs and is generated by these business processes. Develops compelling business cases: Leads the prioritization and development of strong and clear business cases for digital capability investments in support of the roadmap and aligned with the platform strategy. Defines, measures, & achieves business outcomes for highest value (at the lowest cost) digital capabilities. Brings an external view: Actively maintains awareness of external drivers and relevant technology trends in the domain of their product ownership, bringing new ideas. Knows what value looks like: Understands where BMS should be competitively differentiated through technology in Medical Affairs, translates business needs into specific business requirements, sees realistic opportunities for technology to add more value, and balances this with a pragmatic understanding of “fit for purpose”. Provide strategic leadership: Builds strong partnerships with senior leaders of Medical Affairs: Is viewed by senior business leaders as an effective partner who plans and delivers digital capabilities, safeguards their digital assets and supports their strategic goals. Recognized as a thought leader and trusted advisor: Influences the strategic thinking of senior business leaders, and helps business leaders to include future digital capabilities into their planning. Builds relationships: Has effective working relationships with all relevant business leaders, is deeply involved with key business activities and forums, is responsible for building and managing effective business partnership at all levels during project execution, and takes full accountability for delivering the value proposition of BI&T. Enables change adoption : Partners with business process owners and change management leads to ensure technology delivery supports effective change management (e.g., release and cutover planning, impact assessment inputs, communications/training enablement, hypercare and support readiness). Ensures the required technical artifacts and inputs are delivered on time for each initiative to maximize adoption and value realization. Leverages the matrix to drive portfolio execution: Demonstrates Matrix leadership by leveraging other functions in delivery of services to Medical Affairs. Such as internal BI&T partners: Core Services, Content Capabilities, Data capabilities and analytics. Empowers delivery teams: Understands accountabilities throughout the portfolio lifecycle, such as gathering requirements from stakeholders, ensuring proper relay to delivery teams, and owning outcomes. Builds empowered and trusting partnerships with delivery team members at all levels including application owners, Cybersecurity, ITQA, etc. Constructively advocates for value: Ensures delivery teams understand how to make the right trade-offs between speed, quality and cost. Connects the business stakeholders with the broader BI&T services. Ensures value is being captured from the entire lifecycle of the investment (from launch through retirement). Demonstrates good judgement in communication: Communicates successes and issues accurately, urgently, and to the right audience, and takes accountability for ensuring effective management of expectations with business leaders. Boldly acts with urgency: Shows courage, tenacity and respect to provoke uncomfortable conversations in order to remove roadblocks to value delivery. Required Experience Requires Bachelor's degree, MBA is strongly preferred. Strong domain expertise in the application of BI&T to Medical Affairs, including a broad understanding of relevant Medical business capabilities (Publications, Scientific Content Management) and how they are enabled by technology solutions and data. 7-10 years of experience in similar roles in Pharmaceuticals IT for Medical Affairs or Commercial functions. Track record of leading the analysis of complex and ambiguous business needs, and integrating those into compelling and actionable strategic plans and investment business cases with global reach. Experience in driving digital capabilities to create a superior customer experience. Demonstrable commitment to assess and apply innovative AI and new technologies to use cases in Medical Affairs, achieving a balance between pragmatic value and transformation. Experience of large-scale application deployments, and how to work with software & consulting partners ensure maximum value and effectiveness. Experience of maximizing value from enterprise BI&T platforms, including Veeva Vault MedComms and iEnvision. Working knowledge of agile methodologies applied to SDLC and IT services. Ability to drive strategic connections between Medical Affairs, Commercial and Clinical Development functions with an enterprise mindset and reimagine digital capabilities. Goal-oriented self-starter with ability to influence teams toward an executable vision. Seasoned line and matrix management skills, with a particular emphasis on energizing and developing experienced IT professionals spread across multiple functions. Demonstrated ability to create and support a dynamic culture of innovation and continuous improvement in line reports and in the matrix. Excellent collaboration, communication, and presentation skills. A network of external advisors and resources. We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. Compensation Overview: Princeton - NJ - US: $166,600 - $201,880 The starting pay range(s) listed above is for full-time employees (FTE). You may also be eligible for additional discretionary incentive cash and stock opportunities. We determine starting pay thoughtfully – carefully considering the nature of the role, required skills, work location, schedule and the knowledge and experience you bring. Final compensation is guided by pay equity principles and applicable employment laws. Compensation programs are reviewed on an ongoing basis and may be adjusted over time to reflect evolving market factors, and individual, team or Company performance. cold_email.subject: Interest in Product Manager, Global Medical Affairs BI&T - Scientific Content & Publications — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Product Manager, Global Medical Affairs BI&T - Scientific Content & Publications opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Sr Manager, Lab Operations Learning and Development
jobs.description: JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY: The Senior Manager, Lab Operations Learning and Development provides tactical building along with long term strategic leadership and direction for all learning, development, and performance enablement initiatives across laboratory operations. This role is responsible for designing, facilitating, and executing comprehensive L&D initiatives that align with strategy that equips lab operations teammates — from entry level employees to senior leaders — with the knowledge, operational skills, and leadership capabilities needed to drive operational excellence and organizational growth. The Manager/Senior Manager, Lab Operations Learning and Development sets the broad framework for learning culture within lab operations, builds scalable development programs, and partners cross-functionally with HR, lab operations senior leadership, and individual lab leaders to ensure the organization has the skills and required to meet current and future business objectives. This role will require a diverse knowledge and skill set as well as require the capacity to initially focus on tangible program builds and execution then evolve to manage and execute more strategically as scope and programs grow. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES : Strategy & Organizational Development Develops and executes innovative L&D strategies to ensure lab operations has the necessary management and leadership competencies to meet business objectives. Sets the overarching framework and strategy for learning and development across lab operations, aligned to organizational goals, HR timelines, and department priorities. Assesses developmental needs across lab operations teams; identifies management skills and competency gaps and establishes measures to track progress and effectiveness of the applied L&D program(s). Partners with HR to align employee development with job architecture ladders and career progression frameworks. Stays current on training industry developments, adult learning best practices, and emerging trends in development education. Manages and reports out on the L&D budget for lab operations, including forecasting, vendor spend, and resource allocation to ensure cost-effective program delivery. Defines, tracks, and reports on key L&D metrics and KPIs (e.g., training completion rates, time-to-competency, learner satisfaction, business impact) to senior leadership and stakeholders. Leadership & Manager Development Creates and facilitates leader development programs tailored to new leaders, middle management, and senior-level leaders within lab operations. Facilitates DiSC and/or Clifton Strengths programs across lab operations and ensures sustained adoption and practical application. Drives lab operations-specific management training, including senior leaders accountability for tier meeting structure, accountability frameworks, and operational leadership education. Develops and facilitates a formal mentorship, shadowing, and job rotational framework and structure to support career development and knowledge retention across the organization. Partners with HR to inform on succession planning to help identify high-potential leaders within laboratory operations. Develops a comprehensive, all employee onboarding program that can be used across lab operations and at all levels. Should include introduction to Natera departmental functions, Lab operations overview, product education, sample lifecycle, core mission and values, key resources, etc. Develops onboarding programs for newly promoted or externally hired leaders to accelerate time-to-effectiveness in their roles. Long term develops and implements an internal job shadow and mentorship program focused on retention and career development of employees. Long term develops and manages a Lab Operations internship program to create pro-active talent pipelines from universities and relevant institutions. Training Design & Delivery In partnership with department managers, work with department trainers to facilitate training programs directed at soft skills needed to be an effective trainer. Designs and develops soft skills, leadership, and cross-functional business training using instructor-led, blended, and e-learning formats. Maintains and delivers a centralized cross-functional knowledge base platform specific to Lab operations that is available to employees and managers. Continually refines and improves training curriculum based on participant feedback, quality data, and training evaluations. Researches, evaluates, and manages external training vendors and subject matter expert partnerships as needed. Administers training logistics and coordinates training events, including scheduling, materials, and systems administration. Oversees the administration of the Learning Management System (LMS) for lab ops; ensures training records are maintained. Cross-Functional Programs Facilitates cross-functional training among sub-departments within lab operations to build organizational cohesion and shared expertise. Provides internal consulting to individuals, teams, and departments on training and development opportunities that will enhance performance and career progression. Coordinates training events and supports broader organizational development initiatives as needed. Builds and manages a network of internal subject matter experts (SMEs) to contribute to training content development and ongoing curriculum review. QUALIFICATIONS : Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Organizational Development, Education, or a related field required. 4-6 years of experience in training design, curriculum development, and delivery in a high volume organization required, with at least 2 years in a biotech, pharmaceutical, or clinical laboratory environment preferred. Experience facilitating leadership development frameworks (DiSC, Clifton Strengths, coaching models) required. Experience managing or administering a Learning Management System (LMS) in a regulated environment required. Demonstrated experience building and executing L&D programs through periods of organizational growth and large-scale operational change preferred. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES : Ability to self-start, work independently, and collaborate as a member of various cross-functional teams and committees while adhering to timelines. Ability to translate complex scientific and technical content into accessible, engaging learning experiences for varied audiences. Proven strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills; comfortable presenting to all levels of the organization. Proficient in Microsoft Office and Google Suit products; experience with LMS platforms and e-learning authoring tools preferred. Effective team player with the ability to build trust and influence without direct authority. Commitment to excellence, continuous improvement, and high work product standards. Strong organizational, problem-solving, and analytical skills; ability to manage multiple priorities, projects, and workflows simultaneously. Versatility, flexibility, and willingness to work within a dynamic, fast-paced biotech environment with changing priorities. Strong data literacy; ability to build L&D dashboards, interpret training metrics, and present ROI analysis to senior stakeholders. Experience with competency framework design and behavioral anchoring to support role-based training qualification and performance management. PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT : Duties are primarily performed in an office and laboratory environment. Position requires the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone, and read printed material. Occasional access to laboratory areas may require adherence to applicable safety protocols and PPE requirements. Travel will be required, at up to 50% of the time. May require occasional evening or weekend availability to support training events, system implementations, or global team collaboration across time zones. The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations. Remote USA $133,900 — $166,950 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! For more information, visit www.natera.com . Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws. If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents. jobs.title: Scientist 3 - Translational Medicine (Ophthalmology)
jobs.description: We advance science so that we all have more time with the people we love. Genentech's Translational Medicine OMNI (TM OMNI) team supports the entire R&D portfolio of novel therapies across Ophthalmology, Metabolism, Neuroscience, Immunology, and Infectious Diseases. We develop and implement cutting-edge translational research and biomarker strategies to identify complex disease pathways, validate mechanisms of action, and accelerate clinical trial success. Scientists within our department leverage deep clinical insights to drive next-generation target identification and champion end-to-end biomarker execution, from initial discovery to final data interpretation. Opportunity: We are seeking a talented and highly motivated Scientist 3 to join Genentech’s Translational Medicine (TM) team on-site at our South San Francisco campus. In this role, you will partner with cross-functional R&D teams to drive translational research for next-generation therapeutic targets and provide critical biomarker support for glaucoma neuroprotection programs throughout the drug development lifecycle. This position uniquely bridges data science and the wet lab, requiring a blend of computational skills to interpret high-dimensional datasets and bench-level expertise to design and execute validation experiments. This is a hands-on, high-impact opportunity for a scientist eager to apply their training to drive foundational science and establish a new disease area at Genentech, navigating the complexities of ophthalmic drug development within a deeply collaborative environment. As an integral member of our dynamic team, you will: Analyze high-dimensional datasets (e.g., proteomics, transcriptomics) generated from clinical and preclinical samples to discover novel therapeutic targets and candidate biomarkers. Design and execute experiments using disease-relevant in vitro human cell models to translate data-driven insights into functional biology. Lead and coordinate exploratory clinical studies in partnership with internal and external collaborators to advance translational research and discover clinical biomarkers. Collaborate closely with cross-functional R&D partners, including Research Biology, Computational Sciences, Tissue Genomics & Proteomics, Biostatistics, Clinical Pharmacology, and Bioanalytical Sciences. Develop and qualify custom assays (e.g., Simoa, NULISA) for biomarkers of interest, moving beyond standard commercial kits to build bespoke solutions for pipeline programs. Communicate insights effectively across the organization and the broader scientific community through high-quality reports, presentations, and peer-reviewed publications. Who You Are: The ideal candidate will bring: A PhD in Biological Sciences (including neuroscience, immunology, cell biology, or a related field) with 0–4 years of relevant post-graduate experience. Exceptional candidates without a PhD but with an equivalent track record of rigorous scientific experience are also encouraged to apply. While clinical or translational experience in retinal biology is preferred, it is not required. We welcome applicants with broad biological expertise who are eager to apply their skills to a new disease area. A proven track record of executing both wet-lab experiments and bioinformatic analyses to answer complex biological questions, as demonstrated through a strong peer-reviewed publication record. Deep technical wet-lab expertise in preclinical/clinical sample analysis and molecular biology techniques (including cell culture, ELISA, qPCR, and NGS/transcriptomics). Computational proficiency with hands-on experience programming in R or Python to apply biostatistical and bioinformatics methods to high-dimensional datasets. Demonstrated scientific independence, outstanding organizational and teamwork skills, scientific curiosity, and exceptional communication abilities with a clear passion for translating science into life-changing therapies. Relocation benefits are not available for this posting. The expected salary range for this position based on the primary location of California is $100,400 -186,400. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law. A discretionary annual bonus may be available based on individual and Company performance. This position also qualifies for the benefits detailed at the link provided below. Benefits Genentech is an equal opportunity employer. It is our policy and practice to employ, promote, and otherwise treat any and all employees and applicants on the basis of merit, qualifications, and competence. The company's policy prohibits unlawful discrimination, including but not limited to, discrimination on the basis of Protected Veteran status, individuals with disabilities status, and consistent with all federal, state, or local laws. If you have a disability and need an accommodation in relation to the online application process, please contact us by completing this form Accommodations for Applicants .

cold_email.subject: Interest in Scientist 3 - Translational Medicine (Ophthalmology) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Genentech / Roche Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Scientist 3 - Translational Medicine (Ophthalmology) opportunity with Genentech / Roche at Genentech / Roche.

I am especially interested in the lab's combination of neurotechnology, quantitative biology, and questions about brain-wide computation. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background spans biology, scientific programming, and reproducible data pipelines, and I am eager to apply that mix in a neuroscience setting.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

This functional team has the responsibility for enabling new and existing manufacturing operational capabilities through the design, development, and support of manufacturing equipment systems. As a Design Engineer, you will leverage your experience and design knowledge to create solutions to manual, semi-automated, and automated manufacturing problems for Illumina consumables. In addition, you will own and support the deployment of various design solutions to NPI programs throughout the planning, requirements, specification and design, verification, validation and production release phases of capital equipment projects. Job Duties and Responsibilities: Develop NPI and Manufacturing solutions by designing and modifying equipment and fixtures for fabrication, build, assembly, documentation, installation, and release Capture and convert the needs of various NPI and Manufacturing programs and projects into appropriate, manufacturable, and reliable design solutions Follow through on transfer and release of NPI products into manufacturing, track issues, and implement corrective design actions Conduct detailed tolerance analyses on assemblies Participate in troubleshooting and failure analyses Collaborate with stakeholders and colleagues within Process Engineering, Product Development, Systems Engineering, Manufacturing, Software, Validation, Quality, and EH&S Demonstrate ability to multi-task, stay organized, and incorporate feedback in a fast-paced environment Successfully meet programs milestones while breaking down barriers to design creative solutions and achieve results Experience: Demonstrated knowledge of mechanical engineering design principles and practices - Form, fit, tolerance stack analysis, GD&T, drafting standards, FEA, design for assembly, design for manufacturing, etc. Experience designing and working with mechanisms, such as clutches, gear trains, cams, and linkages or selection of electromechanical components such as motors, power transmission components and sensors Experience in designing and troubleshooting electro-mechanical/mechatronic assemblies Knowledge in material manufacturing methods including, but not limited to: machining, sheet metal forming, additive manufacturing, and injection molding Fluent in SolidWorks CAD software or similar Experience in FDA regulated markets is a plus Experience in statistical practices and methods is a plus Education: Typically requires a minimum of 2-3 years of related experience in biotech, medical device, or IVD field with a Bachelor’s degree; or 1-2 year(s) with a Master’s degree Engineering Degree preferred in Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering or equivalent The estimated base salary range for the Engineer 2, Automation Design (Mechanical) role based in the United States of America is: $90,000 - $135,000. cold_email.subject: Interest in Engineer 2, Automation Design (Mechanical) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Illumina Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Engineer 2, Automation Design (Mechanical) opportunity with Illumina at Illumina.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning. You’ll partner closely with Marketing, Growth, Product, Design, Communications, and Engineering to operationalize web work in a fast-moving environment. This is a hands-on production role: you’ll build pages while owning the details, quality, communication, and follow-through that make launches run smoothly. This role is based in San Francisco. The role requires a hybrid schedule, with employees in the office Monday through Wednesday. jobs.description: Role Summary The Global Clinical Supply (GCS) Interactive Response Technology (IRT) Implementation Analyst is a position within Global Central Operations Network (GCON) GCS Strategic Hubs (GSH) team and will be based in Costa Rica. The IRT Implementation Analyst will be reporting to the GSH Team Lead in Costa Rica, with a matrix reporting relationship to the Engagement Leader, IRT Global Oversight Team (IGOT) within Clinical Supply Informatics & Technology (CSIT). GCS manages the execution of supply chain strategies to deliver Investigational Medicinal Product to patients involved in Pfizer’s clinical research trials across the globe. IGOT is a well-established high performing team within Pfizer's GCS unit striving to deliver best in class IRT systems providing randomization and drug management capabilities in support of Pfizer's dynamic investigational product portfolio. The patients we serve are our number one priority and IGOT aims to employ the highest quality standards across our internal and vendor IRT solutions. As part of an innovative clinical supply chain, we routinely challenge the status quo in efforts to optimize our systems and processes. The IRT Implementation Analyst is an individual contributor who performs defined implementation activities under the direction of an accountable IRT Lead, Design Lead, or functional lead. Responsibility and independence will expand progressively based on completion of required training, demonstrated proficiency, and role readiness. Job Description The IRT Implementation Analyst is a new role within the IRT IGOT that will support requirements and system development. The implementation of this dedicated function within IGOT is intended to ensure the delivery of high-quality IRT systems through focused system expertise while improving velocity in support of Pfizer’s evolving portfolio. The IRT Implementation Analyst will go through a robust onboarding and technical training period where they will partner closely with IGOT’s IRT Leads and Design Leads to develop proficiency in conducting preliminary protocol assessments, eliciting protocol requirements, and designing and configuring study builds on Pfizer’s internal IRT system. The IRT Implementation Analyst will support Implementation team members by organizing and facilitating meetings, capturing meeting minutes, creating and reviewing IRT supportive documents, and delivering investigator meeting slides to clinical teams and site personnel. IRT Implementation Analysts will also support line leads in collaborating with study team and supply chain personnel to resolve issues, understand how study requirements are configured and supported post study go-live, and for ongoing studies, be available for guidance on IRT resupply settings and any requisite system amendments. The IRT Implementation Analyst will also learn how quality investigations, Correction Action/ Preventive Action (CAPA) commitments and continuous improvements, Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) review and revision activities, support regulatory inspections, and limited duration teams are created and executed. For this position candidates will need to have excellent technical and analytical thinking skills, be a creative problem solver, and have a strong commitment to quality to successfully deliver optimal IRT systems across a diverse and dynamic portfolio. What You Will Achieve Support the delivery plan for IRT configuration and testing activities. Support the elicitation and documentation of system requirements for new and amended studies in partnership with the study team. Support the development and execution of User Acceptance Testing (UAT) test plans. Participate in cross line initiatives, quality investigations, SOP development, and process improvement. Will be trained to create IRT supportive documents and deliver investigator meeting slides to clinical teams and site personnel. Support for Assigned Projects: Aid in the design, delivery, and management of activities related to assigned projects. Participate in study and functional meetings and provide clear updates on assigned activities, risks, actions, and deliverables under the guidance of the accountable IRT Lead, Design Lead, or functional lead. Coordinate and execute assigned activities across multiple studies or projects, manage competing priorities, and meet agreed timelines and quality expectations. Use appropriate metrics to measure progress on goals, develop and implement key performance indicators (KPI) to track and measure progress towards strategic goals and ensure value-driven outcomes. Adapt and response quickly to changing business needs and deliver results in challenging first-time situation. Provide timely and actionable insights to stakeholders to support decision-making and strategic planning. Apply approved procedures, standards, and training to resolve routine issues within assigned activities; identify risks, exceptions, or unclear requirements and escalate them promptly to the accountable lead. Attend periodic meetings with teams in other global time zones outside of normal work hours. Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements): Associate degree or BA degree in computer science, life science, or business field desired in biopharma industry 1-3 years demonstrated and relevant experience in pharma/biotech and cross-functional team Possess excellent English language written and verbal communication Interpersonal, collaboration and business partnership capabilities required Comfortable working with a global team, partners, and customers in a change agile environment Bonus Points If You Have (Preferred Requirements): Clinical supply chain, project management, business analysis, and/or continuous improvement experience Adaptability to changing priorities and requirements Ability to work in a fast-paced environment Organizational Relationships Reports to GSH Team Lead in Costa Rica, with a matrix reporting relationship to the Engagement Leader – IRT of Clinical Supply Informatics & Technology (CSIT). Partners with various functional lines within the Global Clinical Supply organization. This is a hybrid position based onsite at the Pfizer San Jose, Costa Rica site. cold_email.subject: Interest in Interactive Response Technology Implementation Analyst — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Interactive Response Technology Implementation Analyst opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin
